request.spec:
People can be pasted in as lines of name,grade,terms,contact into an import box (the last two may
be absent or blank). Every line is checked first with exactly the person form's rules (names, aliases,
contacts, grades, terms; a name or contact repeated within the paste is an error): if any line
fails, an error shows on the box and nothing is imported; otherwise every person is added in order,
each as the form would add them (PERSON_ADDED with the same fields). Show how many were added.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
People can be pasted in as lines of name,grade,terms,contact into an import box (the last two may
be absent or blank). Every line is checked first with exactly the person form's rules (names, aliases,
contacts, grades, terms; a name or contact repeated within the paste is an error): if any line
fails, an error shows on the box and nothing is imported; otherwise every person is added in order,
each as the form would add them (PERSON_ADDED with the same fields). Show how many were added.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added the people import box. **1 of the 4 spec tests passes.** The other 3 stop on steps the import doesn't touch: two because of a mistake in the spec, one because of an existing claim rule.

**What I built**
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/import-people` (`import-people.POST.yml`). `ValidateImport` checks every line first, using exactly the same rules as the person form. A line may leave out the terms and contact or leave them blank, blank lines are skipped, and a name or contact repeated within the paste is an error. `ImportPeople` then checks each line against the sheet the same way the form does: names, aliases and the sheet's tree, and contacts. If any line fails, the response is a 400 that names the line, and nothing is written to the store or the audit file. Otherwise each person is added in order with the same `PERSON_ADDED` line and the rollup lines that follow it. Viewers are already refused by the existing `RefuseViewerChanges` filter.
- **Reuse:** I didn't copy the form's rules. `ValidatePerson.check` and `AuditPersonAdded.record` are now package-private static helpers. OfficeFloor won't start if a step class has more than one public method, so they couldn't be public.
- **Front end:** `features/people/import.slot.tsx` adds the box (`import-people`), the submit button (`import-submit`), the count added (`import-added`) and the error (`import-error`). The error clears when the box is edited or submitted again.

**Test results from `bin/e2e`**
- **"import people": passes.** This is the main test of the feature, including all the refusal cases and the full audit sequence.
- **"scenario 1" and "scenario 2": fail on a mistake in the spec.** At lines 234 and 641 the spec expects `sheet-parent` to show the literal text `"__SHEET__-p"`. That placeholder was never replaced with the sheet id, so the screen correctly shows `<sheetId>-p`. Every import step before those lines went through as expected. I can't edit the spec and shouldn't make the app show the placeholder, so this needs fixing in the spec.
- **"scenario 3": fails at line 987,** where it adds a claim for Eve dated 2026-03-01. The server refuses it with "The period P2 is closed". The sheet's 10-day terms only start on 2026-04-05, so the default terms apply on 03-01, and that pushes the due date into P2, which is closed. A person added through the normal person form (no import) gets the same refusal. So this comes from the existing claim and period rules: either the spec expects different behaviour there, or that's a separate change. I didn't change those rules because this request doesn't cover them.

The scenario 1 and 2 fixes belong in the spec. For scenario 3, someone needs to decide whether the spec or the existing rule should change.
